title: What Is the Ocean?
keyIdea: The ocean is a huge body of salt water that covers most of Earth. It has a shore, shallow water and deep water. It is a habitat for sea animals. Puddles, baths and swimming pools are not oceans.
familyTip: Look at a globe or map together. Point to the big blue parts and say 'ocean'. Ask: 'Is our bath an ocean? Why not?'

visual.caption: Ocean or not? Drag each clue, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: build shore–shallow–deep, sort ocean vs not, mark salt water, and catch ocean myths.

kid: The ocean is huge salt water that covers most of Earth.
Near the land is the shore, then shallow water, then deep water farther out.
Ocean water is salty. Many ponds and puddles are fresh water.
Whales and many fish live in the ocean. A bathtub or swimming pool is not an ocean.
adult: Ages 5 to 7 geography/science: ocean as a vast salt-water body and habitat; shore, shallow, deep; waves. Distinct from listing where water is found — here the focus is what the ocean is.
Common mistakes: calling every wet place an ocean; thinking ocean water is fresh; mixing pools/baths with oceans; saying whales live in fields; thinking the ocean is small.
In the lab your child builds zones, sorts ocean vs not, marks salt vs fresh, places a whale in the ocean, shows waves and vast size, then faces challenge traps for those slips.

practice.hint: Think of the vast blue parts on a globe.
practice.explain: The ocean is a huge natural body of salt water. Puddles and baths are not oceans.

practice.hint: Seas and oceans taste of salt.
practice.explain: Ocean water is salty. Tap water and juice are not ocean water.

practice.prompt: A chart marks {n} shore signs and {k} deep-water signs. How many ocean-zone marks in all?
practice.hint: Add the shore marks and the deep-water marks.

practice.prompt: {n} whale pictures and {k} puddle pictures. How many ocean-animal homes?
practice.hint: Count only the whale homes — whales live in the ocean.
practice.explain: {n} whale pictures are ocean homes. Puddles are not oceans.
Deep water lies farther from the shore. Sand and cups are not the deep ocean.

pool.explain: Whales live in the ocean habitat, not fields or toy boxes.
Pools are not oceans. Oceans are vast natural salt-water bodies.

pool.hint: Watch the top of the water.
pool.explain: Waves move on the surface of the ocean.

pool.prompt: Why isn’t a puddle an ocean?
choices: it is tiny and usually fresh
pool.hint: Compare size and salt. Think about the ocean carefully.
pool.explain: Puddles are tiny and usually fresh. Oceans are huge and salty.

pool.prompt: A poster shows {n} ocean animals. How many ocean animals?
pool.hint: Count the ocean animals on the poster.

pool.prompt: {n} seas are marked salty and {k} puddles are fresh. How many salty seas?

pool.hint: Think beach or coast. Think about the ocean carefully.
pool.explain: The shore is where the ocean meets the land.

pool.prompt: Which list is all about the ocean?
choices: puddle, toy box, dry rock only
pool.hint: Ocean traits: salt, size, habitat, waves.
pool.explain: Salt water, waves and deep water describe the ocean. Baths and fields do not.
